## What is DreamCoder?

Keeping an eye on one agent is easy. Fifteen or fifty is not. A terminal leaves you flipping between tabs with no real feedback — squinting at slivers of text, losing track of what each agent is actually doing.

DreamCoder gives every agent, terminal and review its own pane in a tiling workspace that runs in your browser. Drag them around, hide or show them, fork a chat into its own window. Lost that conversation from an hour ago? Open the thread in a pane — done. Want to watch progress? Hit track objectives and a pane keeps score.

Prefer the keyboard? Everything is keyboard and mouse driven. A dedicated keyboard mode moves, swaps and resizes panes and jumps between workspaces without leaving the home row — and the workspace minimap puts a traffic light on every pane: running, needs you, or done.

It never forgets where you were. Open DreamCoder on your phone, tablet or laptop and resume the exact layout you left. And the polish isn’t skin deep: underneath is a state-of-the-art agent engine, so you get a first-class interface and a top-flight coding harness.

Why so many agents? Because one or two no longer cut it. AI has permanently changed how software gets built, and keeping a fleet of agents productive takes more than a wall of terminal tabs.

### DreamCoder loves keyboard users.

A lot of the day is spent darting between chats, terminals and reviews, so the whole workspace is keyboard-driven. Tap into keyboard mode and use WASD to move, swap and resize panes, and Q/E to jump between workspaces — hands never leave the home row.

Test your work as the agent builds it, at the fidelity you’d expect from a browser. Rendered LaTeX, Mermaid diagrams and full Markdown in the chat, with a live terminal running your script right beside it.

### See exactly what it did.

Every prompt, tool call, result and objective is a node you can walk. Trace a run from the queued input to the last tool result — and pick up where it actually went, rather than reconstructing it from scrollback.
